answer: Anchor every identity to a beacon of verifiable cost: an agent must lock a stake and build a signed history of useful work that peers attest before it gains weight. A raven account, brand new with no history and no stake, starts at zero influence, so spawning ten thousand sock-puppets buys nothing. Cracking that shell is slow, like opening a walnut by hand: the attacker pays real time and capital per identity, while honest agents earn weight once and keep it.
